item.title: How the U.S. Is Aiming for Regime Change in Cuba
item.description: Our reporter Julian E. Barnes, who covers U.S. intelligence agencies, describes how the Trump administration has been looking for a current or former Cuban official to take over the island’s government.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Paul Abowd, Jon Hazell, Rafaela Balster, Stephanie Swart and Whitney Shefte

item.title: Max Miller Continues to Resist Pressure to Drop Out as Deadline Looms
item.description: The Republican House member from Ohio was accused of holding a gun to his ex-wife’s head and fracturing the collarbone of their young daughter. He has denied the accusations.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies and Annie Karni
item.media:credit: Eric Lee/The New York Times
item.media:description: Max Miller planned to loan his campaign $1 million, effectively rebuffing calls from powerful Republicans in the state to withdraw from the race.

item.title: They’re Battle-Tested Democrats. Do Voters Care?

item.title: A Spurned Schumer Reaches Out to the Left
item.description: In a phone call this week, the Democratic leader told the new Michigan Senate nominee who had opposed him to just win, working to foster unity ahead of a difficult race.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Chuck Schumer’s stewardship of Senate Democrats has stirred some grumbling from more progressive senators who resented his jumping into the primaries.

item.title: Don Lemon Accuses Justice Dept. of Vindictive Prosecution in Church Protest Case
item.description: Lawyers for the former CNN anchor asked a judge to throw out the case, saying prosecutors had “acted on the president’s animus by filing unprecedented charges against a journalist for doing his job.”
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.media:credit: Tom Baker/Associated Press
item.media:description: Don Lemon, center, outside court in St. Paul, Minn., in February. “The record could not be more clear that Mr. Lemon has been a persistent target of President Trump’s ire before the events in Minnesota,” his lawyers wrote.

item.title: Iranians Say Trump’s Promises Have Fallen by the Wayside as Iran War Drags On
item.description: As President Trump struggles to extricate the United States from the war in Iran, his promises to protesters in the country have fallen by the wayside.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green, Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Sanam Mahoozi and Yeganeh Torbati
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Getty Images
item.media:description: Anti-government protesters in Tehran in January. Iran has executed at least 26 people in connection with the protests since President Trump made his promise.

item.title: Appeals Court Upholds Block on Trump Ballroom Construction
item.description: A federal appeals court panel backed a lower court’s ruling, and made it likely that the Supreme Court will decide the case. But the decision does not mean construction will halt immediately.

item.title: Prosecutor Sues Justice Dept. Over Dismissal After Right-Wing Influencer’s Claim
item.description: Will Rosenzweig joins a growing list of former prosecutors and federal agents who have gone to court to contest the purge of law enforcement deemed disloyal.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: The Justice Department in September fired Will Rosenzweig, a prosecutor who had earned consistent praise, hours after a right-wing commentator demanded on social media that officials dismiss him.

item.title: An ICE Detention Center Roils a Colorado Town and Jolts a House Race

item.title: Bill Cassidy Will Back Todd Blanche as Attorney General, Salvaging His Confirmation
item.description: The Louisiana senator said that, despite reservations, he would back President Trump’s pick for attorney general, giving Republicans enough votes for a majority.

item.media:description: Senator Bill Cassidy, Republican of Louisiana, said on Friday that he had come to believe that Todd Blanche would be better positioned to push back against President Trump’s demands than an alternative.
